digest.component_or_area: code-review gate and LLM runner model routing
propositions: Each of five LLM-calling steps in code-review.yaml declares a model class (frontier or standard) but every declaration is silently ignored at runtime; all nine observed calls execute on cfg.model instead of their declared class.
PydanticAIRunner.run discards req.config and resolves the model only from self._config, so per-step model assignments computed by RunnerAgentStep never reach the resolver.

The usage log records only the prompt name (op) and not the step id, making it impossible to attribute calls to their originating step when a prompt is used by multiple steps (e.g., code-review-base used by base step and batch finder).

Step 0 (observability) must record step id and declared model class token in usage logs via a ContextVar, making pre-fix defects visible as data rather than requiring inference from absence of evidence.

The wiring fix requires substituting req.config.model into the runner's config when they differ, following the existing documented contract for per-call overrides (already used for temperature and usage_limits).

Live proof: under a class table whose values differ from cfg.model, pre-fix runs show all nine calls on cfg.model while post-fix shows declarations honored per step, with step attribution now visible in usage logs.
